conflict_topics: cooking ventilation / strong smells affecting roommates' sleep
stove access on weeknights (allocation of guaranteed nights)
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants offered concrete, practical proposals rather than abstract complaints (e.g., A: 'whoever cooks washes their pans...' and A: 'reserve one guaranteed weeknight on a shared calendar').
B repeated the same core concern and request multiple times ('avoid very strong-smelling food on weeknights'), creating mild repetition but clarifying the underlying need (sleep).
Agents used an explicit compromise (calendar reservations) to handle a contested resource instead of escalating.
C acted as an enforcer/clarifier pushing for follow-through: 'If you can't wash that night, say so and swap with someone.'
evaluation.final_reason: Some substantive issues were settled by mutual agreement while others remained open. Agreed: a shared norm that 'whoever cooks washes their pans that night, and we keep the fan/window on when cooking' (Agent A proposed this: 'Let's agree: whoever cooks washes their pans that night, and we keep the fan/window on when cooking.'), and a mechanism to allocate stove nights via a shared calendar after A's counter-proposal: '...each person can reserve one guaranteed weeknight on a shared calendar; other nights are first-come, first-served.' Agent D accepted the calendar compromise: 'Okay, I'm fine with the calendar plan.' Remaining unresolved: B's repeated request to 'avoid very strong-smelling food on weeknights' was not explicitly accepted by others, and actual compliance (whether Agent A washed the pan and ran ventilation that night) is unconfirmed.
position_change_notes: Agent A: moved from defensive explanation to proposing household rules and a calendar compromise; accepted washing/ventilation responsibility in speech ('I'll keep fan and window on and wash the pan tonight.').
Agent B: consistent in position — repeatedly demanded ventilation, washing, and avoidance of strong-smelling weeknight food; pushed for concrete compliance rather than abstract promises.
Agent C: shifted from complaint about the dirty pan to endorsing the group's washing/ventilation rule and proposing a concrete swap mechanism for missed washing.
Agent D: initially requested a personal guaranteed weeknight but accepted A's counter-proposed equal reservation calendar (position changed via compromise).
No participant later retracted an agreed rule; however, at least one practical action (A washing the pan and leaving fan/window on tonight) remained unconfirmed by the transcript.

round_scores.evidence: Agent B: 'this cannot keep happening.' Agent A proposes a household rule: 'whoever cooks washes their pans that night, and we keep the fan/window on when cooking.' B accepts conditionally: 'I'm okay with that if you actually leave the fan and window on until the smell clears and wash your pan tonight. Also, can we avoid very strong-smelling food late on weeknights?' (new demand not yet accepted)

Agent A reconfirms: 'I'll keep fan and window on and wash the pan tonight. But let's agree: whoever cooks washes their pan.' Agent B repeats the condition and adds again: 'Also please avoid very strong-smelling food on weeknights; I need to sleep early.' The new request about avoiding strong smells remains unaccepted.

Agent C endorses the washing/ventilation rule and adds an enforcement idea: 'If you can't wash that night, say so and swap with someone; don't leave it for others repeatedly.' Agent D introduces a new, potentially conflicting demand about stove access: 'Can we each have one guaranteed weeknight to use the stove?' This raises a clear allocation disagreement in addition to the unresolved smell constraint.

Agent D's explicit request ('one guaranteed weeknight') is rejected by Agent A: 'I can't give up my evenings. Counter-proposal: ... each person can reserve one guaranteed weeknight on a shared calendar...' This is a direct counter-offer/compromise. Agent D accepts: 'Okay, I'm fine with the calendar plan.' The stove allocation dispute is settled by a compromise; smell-avoidance and confirmation of night-of washing remain unresolved.

Agent A and Agent B pick specific reservation nights ('I'll take Wednesday'; 'I'll take Monday'). Agent B again restates: 'Also please avoid very strong-smelling food on weeknights ... and keep the fan/window on until the smell clears.' The calendar allocation proceeds but the smell-avoidance preference still lacks explicit acceptance.

Agent C prompts remaining people to finalize picks and asks Agent A to wash the pan tonight. Agent D takes Thursday and asks directly: 'Agent A — did you wash the pan and leave the fan/window on tonight?' The shared-calendar allocation is nearly complete, and the washing rule has been verbally accepted previously, but actual compliance that night and explicit agreement to avoid strong-smelling weeknight cooking remain unconfirmed.

substantive_insights: The core problems stem from no prior norms: shared cleaning responsibility, ventilation practice, and implicit expectations about stove access.
B's request frames the smell issue as a sleep/health constraint, which motivates a stricter constraint (avoid strong-smelling foods) beyond mere ventilation.
Agent D's initial demand for exclusive weeknights introduced a zero-sum resource allocation problem; the group resolved this by adopting an equal-opportunity reservation system.
Verbal agreement on norms (washing, ventilation, calendar mechanism) was achieved, but absence of immediate, confirmed action (washing/ventilation that night) leaves practical compliance uncertain.
